text:
maya: Hey team, new EKS cluster in ap-northeast-4 (apne4) finished provisioning. GPU nodepool (a100-spot) came up but we're seeing intermittent pod networking timeouts when pulling images and occasional kubelet node-not-ready flaps. Anyone oncall to sanity-check? :wave:
owen: On it. Can you paste `kubectl get nodes -o wide` and the CNI daemonset logs?
maya: Sure — excerpt below (trimmed):
```
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide
NAME                              STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION   INTERNAL-IP   EXTERNAL-IP   OS-IMAGE
ip-10-0-8-12.ec2.internal         Ready    <none>   12m   v1.25.6   10.0.8.12     <none>        Ubuntu 22.04
ip-10-0-9-34.ec2.internal         NotReady <none>   10m   v1.25.6   10.0.9.34     <none>        Ubuntu 22.04
ip-10-0-10-56.ec2.internal        Ready    <none>   9m    v1.25.6   10.0.10.56    <none>        Ubuntu 22.04
```
And CNI error snippet:```
E0330 12:04:21.123456 1 cni.go:214] failed to setup pod network: failed to add veth pair: operation not permitted
W0330 12:04:22.789012 1 ipamd.go:501] ENI capacity check throttled, retrying
```
Also seeing image pull latency ~2-3m for some registry regions.
sara: Two quick checks: 1) Are node ENI limits being hit for these instance types? 2) CNI MTU mismatch between VPC (9001 for jumbo) and pod network (1500) can cause fragmentation; any NAT gateways in the path?
maya: ENI usage looks fine for a100 nodes (low). VPC subnets set to jumbo MTU 9001 — we used Cilium in eBPF mode with default MTU=1500 from the chart. That could explain fragmentation.
own: If MTU mismatch is the likely cause, set cilium.agentConfig.mtu to 9001 in the helm values and redeploy. But we should validate path MTU with iperf tests between nodes first.
alex: I ran a quick iperf3 test between two worker nodes — throughput looked OK but packet retransmits spiked for >1400 bytes. Suggest setting mtu=8900 to leave room for GENEVE headers.
maya: Noted. Also curious about kubelet flaps — logs show eviction due to ephemeral storage pressure on one node: `eviction manager: attempting to reclaim ephemeral-storage` — but total disk used is only ~40%. Any kubelet config overrides?
sara: Could be container runtime overlayd space accounting issue with large model caches (/var/lib/models). We should bind-mount a larger EBS volume to /var/lib/models and set kubelet eviction thresholds to 15% for ephemeral-storage in the node config.
devops-bot: Automated smoke tests status: images-pull-check PASS (average 45s), pod-sched-check FAIL (1/10 pods hit CNI timeout), nodelist-stability WARN (oscillation detected: 2 nodes flapped in last 15m). Logs uploaded: https://internal.artifacts/redwood/apne4-1958765432/logs.tar.gz
owen: Plan proposal — quick ops steps (will run in this order):
1) Patch Cilium MTU to 8900 and roll daemonset with maxUnavailable=1.
2) Run iperf3 MTU sweep and capture retransmit stats.
3) Add a PersistentVolume backed EBS (gp3) to model cache path, update DaemonSet to bind-mount /var/lib/models.
4) Increase kubelet eviction threshold ephemeral-storage to 15% in the launch template userdata (node bootstrap) for the next nodegroup scale-up; cordon+drain problematic node and reprovision if necessary.
5) Change spot fallback: add one reserved a100 on-demand node in the pool as a fallback for registry pulls (to reduce image pull tail latency).
Any objections?
maya: Sounds good. Two questions: how long for step 1 rollout (we're in prod-ish test)? Also cost impact for adding reserved on-demand node — we need to estimate monthly.
alex: Step 1 should be a rolling restart, ~2-3m per node with maxUnavailable=1 for the daemonset — so ~20-30m for 10 nodes. Reserved a100 estimate: ~ $10k/mo (very rough) — but we can use a single smaller on-demand cache-proxy (c5n-type) to host registry cache + pull-through; much cheaper (~$500/mo).
sara: Alternative: deploy a regional pull-through registry (Harbor) on a small reserved instance and use node-local cache (registry cache + crictl prefetch job) — reduces cross-AZ pulls and cut egress. Lower cost than reserved GPU.
maya: Let's do Cilium MTU change now (owen if you can run it), then set up registry cache as next sprint item. I'll cordon the flaky node and attach extra EBS per step 3 after MTU change. :thumbsup:
owen: Will push MTU patch now, updating helm values and kicking a rolling restart. I’ll post helm values and command after apply.
(10 minutes later)
own: Applied `helm upgrade cilium cilium/cilium -f values-mtu-8900.yaml --namespace kube-system` with maxUnavailable=1. Patch diff: `agent.mtu: 8900`
nowen: iperf sweep results: retransmits drop by ~90% at 8900 MTU vs 1500. Pod CNI timeouts reduced in the next 10m window.
maya: Great — I'm cordoning the NotReady node and attaching a 500Gi gp3 EBS for /var/lib/models, will drain and restart model cache daemon.
alex: I'll spin up a tiny registry-cache instance and expose it with internal LB; will add instructions for imagePullSecrets fallback and prefetch job.
sara: Postmortem checklist items: - MTU mismatch documented in region playbook - Add MTU check to cluster-provider validation script - Add registry-cache as recommended pattern for new GPU clusters - Update cost section: recommended pull-through cache vs reserved GPU fallback
maya: Thanks all. Tagging infra runbook: @owen @alex please add the config diffs to the apne4 onboarding doc. Closing thread when artifacts uploaded. :white_check_mark:
